items.q: What does Ross Edgley take from Camus's Sisyphus?
items.a: **The struggle alone is enough** to fill a man's heart, so **pick your suffering**.

items.q: What two fuels does Edgley use on long swims?
items.a: **Gratitude** and darker **"f-you" self-talk**: diesel or petrol, both work.

items.q: What happened to harsh self-talk after ~114 days?
items.a: It **stopped working**; he needed a **gentler** fuel.

items.q: Which motivation is strongest, per Huberman?
items.a: Motivation tied to someone **of you**, like your unborn child, beats an **abstract cause**.

items.q: What happens to the anterior mid-cingulate cortex when you do hard things?
items.a: It **grows** when you do hard things you don't want to do, and **shrinks** when you avoid them.

items.q: What does narrowing your gaze on a target do?
items.a: It **raises arousal** and helps you **recruit energy**: Edgley's "cyclops mode".

items.q: What does a panoramic gaze do?
items.a: It **relaxes** you and lets you **take in more**.

items.q: What usually ends Edgley's swims physically?
items.a: A **ligament or tendon**, not his aerobic capacity.
Build **general physical preparedness** so **connective tissue** can handle later volume.

items.q: What did months of cold and sleep loss do to his stress response?
items.a: **Habituation**: it still registered, but **without the emotional reaction**.
